skill.description: LabArchives API integration for electronic lab notebook setup, notebook backup, entry creation, attachment upload, and research workflow integrations.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, official LabArchives URLs, or domain-specific identifiers. Confirmed issues involve sensitive network uploads, plaintext credential storage, local backup writes, insecure TLS guidance, and unpinned third-party installation guidance.

remediation.issue: Custom API endpoints can receive credentials and uploaded files.
remediation.suggestion: Require HTTPS, validate LabArchives domains by default, and show a clear warning before allowing custom endpoints.

remediation.issue: Credentials are stored in plaintext config.yaml.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer environment variables or a secret manager, and keep config.yaml ignored by version control.

remediation.issue: Notebook backups can contain sensitive research data.
remediation.suggestion: Set restrictive permissions on backup files and recommend encrypted storage for exported notebooks.

remediation.issue: The guide includes a verify=False TLS example.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the example or replace it with certificate bundle configuration and a strong production warning.

remediation.issue: Third-party installation guidance is not pinned.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the labarchives-py dependency to a reviewed release or commit and document verification steps.

semantic_findings.title: Custom Endpoint Credential Exfiltration Risk
semantic_findings.description: The setup flow accepts a custom API endpoint, and the upload script later sends access credentials and files to config[api_url]. A malicious or incorrect endpoint could collect institutional secrets and research attachments.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The custom endpoint is user-supplied, then used as the base URL for requests.post with credentials and file content. Legitimate custom endpoints exist, but the exfiltration path is concrete.

semantic_findings.title: Plaintext Credential Storage
semantic_findings.description: The setup script writes access_key_id, access_password, user email, and external application password to a local YAML file. The file is chmod 600, but the secrets remain plaintext at rest.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code writes credential fields to config.yaml, and the guide documents those fields. The permission hardening mitigates but does not remove plaintext secret storage risk.

semantic_findings.title: Insecure TLS Verification Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The authentication guide includes a requests example using verify=False. Users may copy this pattern and disable certificate validation for API traffic.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guide explicitly shows verify=False under SSL troubleshooting. It includes a testing warning, but the insecure code is directly copyable.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Third-Party Install Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs users to clone labarchives-py from GitHub and install the current checkout. The guidance does not pin a commit, release, or checksum.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The install steps use git clone followed by local installation without version pinning. This is a common supply-chain risk, although the referenced project may be legitimate.

content.value_statement: Research teams need reliable ways to manage electronic lab notebook data through the LabArchives API. This skill guides setup, backups, entry creation, attachment uploads, and integration planning.
actual_capabilities: Guides LabArchives API authentication and regional endpoint setup.
Provides scripts to create a local configuration file for API credentials.
Lists accessible notebooks and backs up notebook data.
Creates entries, adds comments, and uploads file attachments.
Documents integrations with Protocols.io, Jupyter, REDCap, and scientific tools.
Explains site report and user information API workflows.
limitations: Requires Enterprise LabArchives API access and valid credentials.
Depends on labarchives-py or Python requests for API operations.
Does not validate custom API endpoints beyond user input.
Does not encrypt local backups or configuration files.

use_cases.title: Set Up API Access
use_cases.description: Configure regional endpoints, institutional keys, and user authentication for LabArchives API work.

use_cases.title: Back Up Notebook Records
use_cases.description: Export accessible notebooks with metadata, entries, and optional attachments for approved retention workflows.

use_cases.title: Archive Analysis Outputs
use_cases.description: Create LabArchives entries and attach files from Jupyter, REDCap, Protocols.io, or scientific applications.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Credentials
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me configure LabArchives API access for the US endpoint. Explain each required credential and the safest storage choice.

prompt_templates.title: Back Up One Notebook
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through backing up one LabArchives notebook without attachments. Include the required identifiers and expected output.

prompt_templates.title: Upload Experiment Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a LabArchives entry for an experiment and upload selected data files as attachments.

prompt_templates.title: Design Integration Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a secure workflow that exports Jupyter analysis results to LabArchives with metadata, audit notes, and backup checks.

output_examples.input: I need to set up LabArchives API credentials for my institution.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies required institutional and user credentials, recommends the correct regional endpoint, and explains secure storage options.

output_examples.input: I want to back up a notebook without downloading attachments.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines the user ID and notebook ID requirements, selects metadata-only export, and describes the saved backup result.

output_examples.input: I need to archive Jupyter results in LabArchives.
output_examples.output: The skill proposes an export workflow that creates an entry, attaches the notebook file, and records metadata for traceability.

best_practices: Use environment variables or a secret manager when possible.
Confirm the regional endpoint and require HTTPS for all API traffic.
Store backups in approved encrypted locations with limited access.
anti_patterns: Do not commit config.yaml or notebook backup archives.
Do not disable TLS verification in shared or production workflows.
Do not use custom API endpoints without administrator approval.

faq.question: Does this skill require LabArchives Enterprise access?
faq.answer: Yes. API use requires Enterprise access and administrator-provided API credentials.

faq.question: Can it back up notebook attachments?
faq.answer: Yes. The notebook script can request full backups with attachments or metadata-only exports.

faq.question: Does it store credentials?
faq.answer: The setup script can write credentials to config.yaml with local user-only permissions.

faq.question: Can it upload files to LabArchives entries?
faq.answer: Yes. The entry script uploads selected files to a specified notebook entry.

faq.question: Does it support OAuth integrations?
faq.answer: It documents OAuth concepts for new integrations, but it does not implement a full OAuth client.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
